First time using your VA Education Benefits at Gavilan College? You're in the right place!

excerpts.line: Next up, you need to submit a few documents to the Veterans Resource Center:
window: Apply for FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) at www.fafsa.ed.gov . You may be entitled to financial aid and fee waivers in addition to your GI Bill®. If you need assistance filling these out please stop by the VRC for help.
Next up, you need to submit a few documents to the Veterans Resource Center:
DD FORM 214, MEMBER 4: Send a copy of your DD Form 214 (Member 4) to the VRC at vrc@gavilan.edu vrc@gavilan.edu

VA CERTIFICATE OF ELIGIBILITY (CoE): Send a copy of your VA CoE for Education Benefits to the VRC at vrc@gavilan.edu vrc@gavilan.edu. The VA will mail this to you after you’ve applied for your GI Bill® benefits online. The CoE shows which GI Bill® Chapter you are eligible for and at what percentage. If you don't have it yet, that's okay. Just be sure to send it once you receive it.

President Avila became Gavilan's 8th President upon approval from the Gavilan Joint Community Districts Board of Trustees meeting on Tuesday, July 12, 2022. As Gavilan president, Avila leads a team of senior staff including vice presidents and associate vice presidents of Instruction, Administrative Services, Student Services and the Public Information Office.

President Avila became Gavilan's 8th President upon approval from the Gavilan Joint Community Districts Board of Trustees meeting on Tuesday, July 12, 2022. As Gavilan president, Avila leads a team of senior staff including vice presidents and associate vice presidents of Instruction, Administrative Services, Student Services and the Public Information Office.

Previously, President Avila served as the Vice President of Student Services at Santa Rosa Junior College. He has worked in the community college system for 20 years and has led several successful initiatives to increase college-going rates for underrepresented student populations.

President Avila became Gavilan's 8th President upon approval from the Gavilan Joint Community Districts Board of Trustees meeting on Tuesday, July 12, 2022. As Gavilan president, Avila leads a team of senior staff including vice presidents and associate vice presidents of Instruction, Administrative Services, Student Services and the Public Information Office.

Previously, President Avila served as the Vice President of Student Services at Santa Rosa Junior College. He has worked in the community college system for 20 years and has led several successful initiatives to increase college-going rates for underrepresented student populations.

President Avila holds degrees in Latino studies and business from Fresno State University. A Master in Business Administration from Rockhurst University and a Certificate in Institutional Performance Assessment from Harvard’s Higher Education Institute. He holds a Doctorate in Community College Policy from the University of Maryland.

His administrative experience includes serving as Associate Vice Chancellor of Enrollment Management, Admissions & Records, and Information Systems at State Center Community College District. At West Hills Community College District, he served as Vice President of Student Services and Vice-Chancellor of Institutional Effectiveness & Enrollment Management.
Dr. Avila’s work is grounded in his experiences as an immigrant, English-language learner, and first-generation college student.

window: The Gavilan Student Veterans of America chapter was founded in Fall of 2011 by a group of student veterans interested in helping veterans and families of veterans succeed and adapt to academic life at a community college.

Our club goals include: improving veteran services at Gavilan College, mentoring student veterans, bringing awareness to veteran issues, promoting understanding on campus, and working with the Gavilan extended community to foster veteran success.

As a club we are committed to Service, Scholarship, and being Social. Each semester we aim to do one service project, one event related to academics (scholarship), and at least one social event. See the schedule below to learn more about what we have planned this semester!
For more information about the club inquire in the Veterans Resource Center in Library 109.
